literal: Even if they are of indispensable excellence, things that come so as to diminish (one's honor), abandon them.
translation: Even if they bring indispensable glory, one must abandon those actions that would diminish one's honor.
modern: தவிர்க்க முடியாத பெருமையைத் தருவனவாக இருந்தாலும், தன் மானம் குறையும்படி வரும் செயல்களைக் கைவிட வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme value of personal honor over any worldly achievement. The phrase 'இன்றி அமையாச் சிறப்பின' refers to things of indispensable excellence or greatness that seem absolutely necessary for life. Yet, the poet advises that if obtaining such greatness causes one's self-respect to diminish ('குன்ற'), those opportunities ('வருப') must be firmly rejected ('விடல்'). No amount of glory or success is worth the sacrifice of one's dignity.
